correctness.rationale: Both independent complete integer constructions cover 65,536 spin assignments on each of the two explicitly defined 16-vertex graphs, verify strongly regular adjacency invariants, agree exactly on all 49 cut coefficients, and establish the claimed factored difference by exact arithmetic. Algebraic substitution q=exp(-2K)>0 and the even power give strict positivity for all real nonzero K, equality at K=0. The binomial transform verifies high-temperature order 8 and maximum-cut counts. Finite exhaustive enumeration is a valid proof of this finite instance, and no infinite claim is made.

value.rationale: The rook and Shrikhande graphs are the canonical smallest nonisomorphic pair with the same (16,6,2,2) parameters, so comparing their full zero-field Ising thermodynamics is naturally motivated. The identity proves a uniform strict ordering at all nonzero ferro- and antiferromagnetic couplings, not just a single numerical discrepancy; degree eight is the first distinguished even-subgraph term despite equal first seven coefficients and the antiferromagnetic ground-state multiplicities differ 90 versus 42. This is a meaningful complete finite-system spectral-versus-thermodynamic boundary, not a generic identity or arbitrary temperature sampling.
